instruction: I need to see the rulers to help with alignment. Can you enable them?

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(5); pyautogui.press('esc'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('f10'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('right', presses=2, interval=0.1); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('down', presses=11, interval=0.1); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.explanation: Task requires showing rulers in LibreOffice Impress. The evaluator checks the accessibility tree for ruler elements. Similar difficulty to original - simple UI element visibility task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator logic correctly checks for ruler visibility in the accessibility tree
Complete coverage: instruction requires enabling rulers, evaluator verifies ruler presence
Multi-pattern search increases robustness: checks both <ruler> elements and panels with 'Ruler' in name
Proper error handling with try/except block returns 0.0 on parse failures
No postconfig needed since ruler state persists after being enabled
Data flow is correct: accessibility_tree → XML parsing → element search → score
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Cannot be 100% certain about accessibility tree element naming without empirical testing, but the dual-pattern search (direct <ruler> tags + panel name matching) makes this very likely to work correctly
